title: MVCC building blocks
caption: Writers add row versions to heap pages, readers use a snapshot to pick one version, and background VACUUM removes old versions.

badges.meaning: xact.c asks varsup.c for a transaction id (xid) when the first write happens
heapam.c writes the new tuple version into a heap page
commit emits a WAL record to pg_wal
procarray.c scans running backends and fills the snapshot (xmin, xmax, xip)
HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC looks up commit status in pg_xact and filters heap tuples
autovacuum launches a VACUUM worker (vacuumlazy.c)
pruneheap.c removes dead tuples from the heap page

title: One UPDATE, two readers, VACUUM
caption: Follow the numbers: session A updates a row, session B first sees the old version, then the new one after commit, and VACUUM finally frees the old copy.

badges.meaning: Session A runs UPDATE and gets xid 100 from GetNewTransactionId
heap_update sets xmax=100 on the old tuple and writes a new tuple with xmin=100
Session B starts a SELECT and takes a snapshot where xid 100 is still in progress
HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC shows B the old tuple and hides the new one
Session A runs COMMIT (CommitTransaction)
Commit is written to WAL first, then pg_xact marks xid 100 committed
Session B runs a new statement with a fresh snapshot and sees the new tuple
VACUUM (lazy_scan_heap) finds the old tuple that no snapshot needs
The old tuple becomes LP_DEAD then LP_UNUSED so its space can be reused

title: Heap page and tuple header
caption: Every row version sits in an 8 kB page and carries a small header with xmin, xmax and ctid that the visibility check reads.

badges.meaning: Zoom into one old tuple on the page to see its header
t_xmin: the xid that inserted this version
t_xmax: the xid that deleted or locked this version
t_ctid: points to the newer version of the row
t_infomask: hint bits that cache commit status
